title: Search Results, Facets, and Recovery
editorial_note: Automated dialogue draft from the revised lesson. Review spoken wording and meaning before publishing.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Today we're talking about Search Results, Facets, and Recovery. By the end, you'll know why this matters, how to use it, and what to notice in a real product.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the problem we are trying to understand?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Search is an interaction system: query formulation, interpretation, indexing, ranking, result explanation, filtering, sorting, no-result recovery, and learning from behaviour. People arrive with varied vocabulary and uncertain intent. A result page should help them refine, compare, and recover rather than punish an imperfect first query.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Why does that happen?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Make result labels and filters reflect language people understand. Show useful attributes, distinguish exact from related matches where it matters, and explain active filters. Zero results are a conversation turn: offer spelling help, broader categories, related terms, or a route to human support—not a dead end.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Make retrieval transparent enough to correct
turns.text: What changes when we look at make retrieval transparent enough to correct?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Search quality depends on indexing, query interpretation, ranking, result representation, and recovery. Facets are not decorative filters: each requires reliable metadata, understandable values, meaningful counts, and rules for missing data. A result page should give enough evidence to judge relevance without exposing information the person is not authorised to see.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The result contract includes title, object type, care episode, status, date meaning, matched evidence, and source. Ranking is evaluated on successful downstream resolution, not clicks alone. A recent message may attract a click but be less useful than the current appointment record.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Sensitive snippets and cross-role results obey permission before ranking, avoiding a leak through titles or counts.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Zero-result recovery diagnoses spelling, vocabulary mismatch, incompatible facets, missing permission, and absence of content differently. The interface preserves the query, explains what was searched, offers a reversible broadening step, and hands context to support when necessary. lesson 133 now examines the metadata and taxonomy that make those behaviours trustworthy.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: ecommerce facets?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A “waterproof” facet is misleading when suppliers use inconsistent claims and missing values disappear from results. The interface may appear sophisticated while making comparison less reliable. Facet design begins with metadata provenance and definitions, not the sidebar component.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Design the result set as an evidence surface
turns.text: What changes when we look at design the result set as an evidence surface?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Clarify query, scope, sort, result count, and applied constraints. Each result should help a person predict relevance through distinctive title, snippet, type, source, date, status, and domain metadata. Highlight matches carefully without destroying readability.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Facets represent dimensions people use to narrow decisions. Derive them from the content model and seeking behaviour, show counts where reliable, support multiple selection with clear logic, and keep active filters visible. Do not offer fields with inconsistent or missing metadata as if they were dependable.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Rank with relevance, authority, freshness, personal or task context, and diversity as appropriate. Explain sponsored or personalised influence. Provide alternate sorts when the decision requires recency, price, distance, or another explicit dimension.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: For zero and weak results, preserve the query, explain scope, suggest spelling, synonyms, removed filters, broader categories, or authoritative support. Analyse reformulation and downstream task success. Clicking a result is not proof that search succeeded.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Define a result and facet contract
turns.text: What changes when we look at define a result and facet contract?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Ranking varies by intent. An exact referral identifier favours the authoritative record. A clinic exploration query balances specialty suitability, location, access evidence, and availability without presenting a clinical recommendation. A problem query such as why was my request returned may combine current case state with governed support content.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: One relevance formula cannot serve all three equally.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Every facet has a metadata contract: concept definition, allowed values, multi-selection logic, missing-state treatment, count meaning, source, and owner. Unknown accessibility data stays visible rather than disappearing from the denominator. Applied filters are inspectable and reversible; counts update predictably; narrow results explain the active constraints.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: research repository?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A search for onboarding may need a known study, all research about first use, or an answer to a current question. Results require method, audience, date, product area, and evidence status. Facets are trustworthy only when repository metadata is complete and governed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the harder design decision appear?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Search promises more than ranking: it depends on metadata, permissions, governance, and a recovery service. Senior teams measure successful resolution and harmful false confidence, not clicks alone, and refuse facets whose source data cannot support the claim.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: <! -- Editorial: manual revision; curated product example --

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can we see that in a concrete product situation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Illustrative scenario: an online parts catalogue. A search for a replacement battery returns hundreds of items. Useful results expose compatibility, stock, and uncertainty; facets narrow by device model without erasing the original query. When no exact match exists, explain why and offer a recovery route rather than a blank “no results” screen.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should I notice the next time I use a product?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Run one exact, one exploratory, and one problem-oriented query in the same product. Compare the evidence in each result, then deliberately produce zero results and assess the recovery.
